messages:
anya: ran a few different profiler passes on prod-dedicated for ~10m (low traffic window). goal: measure safe sampling overhead and identify kernel-hotspots that only show up under realistic batching. summary below + snippets.

anya: TL;DR: lightweight microtraces (eBPF stack samples + perfetto timeline slices) add ~0.2–0.6% tail latency p95 on our config; full nsys captures add ~3–6% and blow up p99 in small batches. KV-cache warmups are the biggest source of noisy kernel churn.

mike: can you paste the exact commands you ran? especially nsys flags.

anya: sure — two commands used:
```
# microtrace (low overhead)
sudo perf record -e cpu-clock -F 99 -g -- sleep 600
# perfetto slice capture (user+kernel timestamps)
perfetto --config microtrace_cfg.pbtx --out microtrace.pftrace
```
and for full GPU timeline (nsys):
```
nsys profile --output=full-prod-run --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --duration=600 --sampling=none
```
(we used --sampling=none to force full timeline; also tried sampling=statistical which lowered overhead but missed short kernels)

li: numbers for overhead? you said p95/p99 impact. which baseline?

anya: baseline = no profiler, same canary traffic. measured on a 4xA100 pool, sequence length mix: 64/256/2048. aggregated:
- microtrace (perf+perfetto): +0.2% p95, +0.4% p99 on batching-heavy routes
- nsys (full timeline): +3% p95, +6% p99, with worst-case spikes up to +12% for small-batch (<4) requests
- kernel-level observed: repeated small GEMM launches (fp16->int8 fallback path) and KV cache eviction I/O causing short host->device memcpy spikes.

sam: 12% spike is worrying. but that's for small-batch synthetic? did you see this on real traffic?

anya: yes — the +12% spikes correlate with a rare sequence: mid-size seq (256) that hits a switch in kernel selection (we call it kernel-switchback) + cache miss on prefix KV leading to chained memcpy + rendezvous kernel. shows up ~0.2% of requests, but those are p99 tail events.

mike: any per-kernel timeline? can you paste a tiny perfetto snippet (text) showing timeline?

anya: pasted (condensed):
```
[0.000s] enqueue request
[0.010s] choose kernel kernel_v2_gemm_fp16
[0.0101s] kv_cache lookup -> miss
[0.01012s] host->device memcpy 1.2ms
[0.0114s] kernel switch to kernel_v2_int8_fallback 0.9ms
[0.0123s] postprocess memcpy 0.3ms
```
This extra memcpy + fallback switch explains the spike.

li: suggests two mitigations:
1) sampling guardrail: only full traces when a microtrace indicates a kernel-switchback pattern, and cap full traces to 0.25% of requests per GPU per hour.
2) batch heuristic: delay dispatch for <=3 items by up to 1ms to allow batch coalescing (configurable by model).

mike: both sound reasonable. what's the proposed guardrail config?

anya: quick draft config (json-y snippet):
```
{"profiler": {
  "microtrace_rate": "1/1000",
  "full_trace_condition": "detect(kernel_switchback) && kv_miss",
  "full_trace_cap_per_gpu_per_hour": "10",
  "exponential_backoff": "true",
  "max_concurrent_full_traces": "1"
}}
```
(meaning: microtrace ~0.1% sampled; full traces only triggered by pattern + capped)

sam: ops concerns: 10 full traces/hr per GPU seems high on heavy clusters. suggest per-cluster throttle and a backoff that increases when avg latency climbs. also we need auth/PII scrub for any full capture before leaving host.

anya: agreed. I'd change cap to 3 per GPU per hour + cluster-level cap 15 + automatic scrub pipeline. also we should avoid tracing requests that touch customer private models (private flag).

mike: we should quantify overhead of microtrace under different sequence distributions. can you run a short AB test next week: baseline, perf-only microtrace, microtrace+stackwalk, and nsys-sampled(1/1000). collect p50/p95/p99 + token-cost impact.

anya: adding to my todo. will run on wed 03:00 UTC low-traffic window.

tracebot: uploaded perfetto link: https://perf.redwood/prod/microtrace/2050012345/attach (perm: eng-runtime) :white_check_mark:

li: one more thing — KV cache behavior: the trace shows a lot of tiny KV lookups that fall back to host due to cold prefix. can we add a lightweight prefix-probing cache warmup on request start? 0.2ms added but avoids fallback memcpy 1.2ms in many cases.

anya: noted. I'll prototype a warmup heuristic: if request.seq >= 128 and model.prefetch_enabled then async prefetch first 1K tokens of KV. we need to measure cost/benefit.

sam: when you run AB, tag traces with rollout id and machine id so we can correlate machine-specific kernel selection oddities. also record CUDA driver version + kernel build.

anya: will do. thanks all — will post results and the AB run artifacts in this thread after the Wed run. :sparkles:
